gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-bree-serif: Loosened tracking gives Stentiga a stretched, luxurious look, with crossbars as sturdy as its stems and no hairlines anywhere. Bree Serif's outsized lowercase grounds that polish with bookish warmth.
gen-dafont-stentiga-outfit: Stentiga's wide-set tracking and sturdy crossbars give it a stretched, luxurious look that quickly holds the eye. Stentiga makes the entrance; Outfit's cable-like lines do the steady, friendly talking.
gen-dafont-stentiga-plus-jakarta-sans: Stentiga stretches its tracking wide and gives its crossbars real weight, which feels distinctly refined and luxurious. Plus Jakarta Sans moves crisply and precisely along when the text runs long.
gen-dafont-true-north-fs-hind: Stocky and unapologetic, True North packs a tall middle band into every line, with curves that refuse to close. Hind, a plain sans, handles the reading with strokes steady as string.
gen-dafont-true-north-fs-quicksand: True North packs a tall middle band into each line, giving it a stocky, bold stance. Quicksand, a plain sans, simply traces each letter in one constant, friendly line.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-almendra: Contemporary in attitude, True North stacks a tall middle band into each line, and its curves refuse to close. Almendra's deep, dignified lowercase makes a quietly bookish counterweight beneath it.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-bree-serif: Bold from the very first glance, True North turns a tall middle band into an unmistakably stocky line. Bree Serif takes over the literary refinement, its lowercase generously outsized.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-port-lligat-sla: True North's tall middle band makes every line look stocky, while its curves stubbornly refuse to close. Port Lligat Slab gives paragraphs a literary, traditional feel with porthole-wide counters.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-quando: True North makes its tall middle band the whole story. Quando is sparse and wide-spaced, carrying a tall middle zone of its own, so a slightly larger size suits it.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-amulya: Visitor's gaping e mouths and short ascenders over big bowls give it a nostalgic, pulled-through-a-nozzle digital look. Amulya, the modern sans-serif, tends to benefit from a little extra size.
